chapter: Caravan, Perdido and the first tunes
title: Where and how Caravan was written
summary: Rose recalls Caravan was written in Los Angeles at the Laveda; Tizol is unsure but remembers playing it for Duke and Mills until Mills liked it.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So you told us about Perdido being written on the train. Where was Caravan written? Where were you when you wrote that?
In Los Angeles. We were living over at the Laveda, and you told me they were going to play it on the air that night and for me to listen to it.
Yeah, but I think I wrote it after that, Rose.
No, you wrote it here in Los Angeles.

I don't remember where I wrote it -- whether it was in Los Angeles or New York, when I was with Duke, or what. I know that I wrote the tune, and me and Duke used to play it to Irving Mills, to everybody. We'd sit down and Duke would say, 'Let's get the trombone and play Caravan.' And 'Let's see if it'll I would play it -- I'd play it and say let's get to Irving Mills,' until finally, he liked it, and that's when we came over to the Cotton Club and played it, and this big leader from MGM liked the tune. And that is when he decided to publish it and take care of Caravan."
